claims.citation: New York Herald, 28 August 1866, p. 9, col. 4
claims.verbatim:
Steamship Teutonia (Ham), Hasch[?], Hamburg, Aug 12,
and Southampton 15th, at 9 AM, with mdse and 325[?] passen-
gers, to Kunhardt & Co. Aug 16, lat 49 50, lon 6, saw ship
City of Mobile, from Callao via Queenstown for London;
20th, lat 47 45, lon 37, saw bark Louise Marie (Dan), bound
East.

claims.citation: The Sun (New York), 23 August 1866, p. 1, col. 4
claims.verbatim:
The steamship Allema-
mania, Capt. Traukmann[?], from Hamburg on 18th
inst., arrived at this port last night, and sailed again
this morning for New York, taking £100,000 sterling
($500,000[?]) for the latter port, on American account.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 4 September 1866, p. 9, col. 3
claims.verbatim:
Steamship Allemania (Ham), Trautmann, Hamburg, Aug
19, Southampton 22d, with mdse and 720 passengers, to Kun-
hardt & Co. Experienced strong westerly winds the entire
passage. Aug 29, lat 47 14, lon 46 50, saw a large iceberg;
22d, off Portland, exchanged signals with a Bremen steam-
ship; steering E; Sept 2, 6 AM, saw steamships Teutonia
(Ham), City of Paris (Br), and The Queen (Br).
